brief.scenario: A 58-year-old woman has had a wide local excision of a breast lesion. The examiner will read out the histology during the station. Written findings: a wide local excision of breast tissue, orientated with marking sutures, has been sliced. One slice shows a firm, grey-white mass about 2 cm across with an irregular, spiculated edge radiating into the surrounding yellow fat, giving a star-shaped outline. The cut surface feels gritty. The mass lies close to one margin. No skin or nipple is included.
brief.task: Summarise and interpret the written specimen findings and the histology the examiner reads out, and answer the examiner's questions on grading, receptor status and prognosis.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Summarise the findings before you diagnose, then grade, receptors and prognosis, in that order.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Naming the diagnosis from the first line of the findings and skipping the structured summary.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "This is a wide local excision specimen, orientated with sutures, sliced to show a mass."

grid.label: Specimen summary
grid.fail: Leads with a diagnosis before summarising the findings.
grid.pass: Summarises the specimen and orientation markers, then size, shape, colour, consistency and margins, in order.
grid.high: Picks out the nearest margin and the absence of skin and nipple before offering a diagnosis.

grid.label: Macroscopic diagnosis
grid.fail: Calls a stellate, gritty mass a fibroadenoma.
grid.pass: Stellate, grey-white, gritty mass: most likely invasive carcinoma of no special type.
grid.high: Gives a differential (lobular carcinoma, fat necrosis, radial scar) and says histology will decide.

grid.label: Histology
grid.fail: Cannot say what makes a carcinoma invasive.
grid.borderline: Says it is malignant but cannot say whether it is in situ or invasive.
grid.pass: Nests and glands of pleomorphic cells infiltrating desmoplastic stroma: invasive carcinoma of no special type.
grid.high: Contrasts lobular carcinoma: single-file, discohesive cells with loss of E-cadherin.

grid.label: Nottingham grade
grid.pass: Tubule formation, nuclear pleomorphism and mitotic count, each scored 1–3.

grid.label: Receptor status
grid.pass: Reports ER, PR and HER2, and explains they guide endocrine and anti-HER2 treatment.
grid.high: HER2 immunohistochemistry: 3+ positive, 2+ equivocal needing in situ hybridisation. ER 1–10% is reported as ER low.

grid.label: Prognosis
grid.pass: Nodal status, tumour size and grade, combined in the Nottingham Prognostic Index.
grid.high: Gives the formula: 0.2 × size in cm, plus grade, plus nodal score (1 none, 2 one to three nodes, 3 four or more).

grid.label: Safe conclusions
grid.fail: Gives a definitive diagnosis from the naked-eye specimen alone.
grid.pass: States that the final diagnosis rests on histology and receptor testing.
grid.high: Commits to a most likely diagnosis while naming what would change it.

failures.consequence: Misses the result that decides anti-HER2 treatment.

failures.move: Giving grade as the only prognostic factor.
failures.consequence: Nodal status is the strongest single factor, and it's missing.

failures.move: Skipping the margins when summarising the findings.
failures.consequence: Misses the observation that decides whether re-excision is needed.

recovery.line: Let me describe it first: size, shape, colour, consistency, then its relation to the margins.
Three components, each scored 1 to 3, so totals run from 3 to 9, in three bands.

knowledge.fact: Nottingham grade: tubule formation, nuclear pleomorphism, mitotic count, each 1–3; totals 3–5 grade 1, 6–7 grade 2, 8–9 grade 3.
HER2 IHC: 3+ positive; 2+ equivocal, needs in situ hybridisation.
ER staining in 1–10% of cells is reported as ER low.
NPI = 0.2 × size (cm) + grade + nodal score (1, 2 or 3).
Lobular carcinoma: discohesive single-file cells, loss of E-cadherin.

recall.think: Describe, differential, histology, grade, receptors, prognosis.
recall.say: "I'll describe it before I name it."
do: ER, PR and HER2, then NPI
recall.trap: Naming it before summarising the findings.
recall.finish: Diagnosis, grade, receptors and nodes decide treatment and prognosis.

partner.opening: You have the written findings for a specimen from a 58-year-old woman. Summarise them for me.

reveals.finding: Read out: the H&E section shows nests, cords and gland-like groups of epithelial cells with enlarged, variably sized, hyperchromatic nuclei and scattered mitoses. The groups lie haphazardly in dense, reactive fibrous stroma and extend into the surrounding fat. Ask what this shows.
Read out: HER2 immunohistochemistry shows strong, complete membrane staining around more than 10% of the tumour cells. Ask how this is scored and what it means.
Read out: 2.0 cm, grade 2, 2 of 14 nodes positive.

push.question: What is your differential?
push.expect: Invasive NST, lobular carcinoma, fat necrosis, radial scar.

curveballs.prompt: HER2 is 2+. Is she HER2 positive?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Equivocal: it needs in situ hybridisation before deciding.

curveballs.prompt: The cells are in single file and E-cadherin is negative. Now what?
curveballs.safeAnswer: That points to invasive lobular carcinoma.

curveballs.prompt: The tumour is 0.5 mm from the margin. Is that clear?
curveballs.safeAnswer: I'd give the measured distance and discuss re-excision with the MDT against local margin policy.
